title: Gabriel Luna on How Arnold Schwarzenegger’s Christmas Party Led Him to ‘The Terminal List’ and ‘Dexter: Resurrection’
full_text: Skip to main content Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty’s Next Billion-Dollar Mogul close By Brian Davids Plus Icon Brian Davids Writer PickYourBrian Follow Sign Up View All November 18, 2026 8:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gabriel Luna Sela Shiloni Logo text [This story contains spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection seasons two, episode three, “Live Free and Die” and The Terminal List season two.] Gabriel Luna once told The Hollywood Reporter that he wouldn’t trade the friendships he made on the underappreciated Terminator: Dark Fate for the brighter fate of a billion-dollar box office haul. Chief among them was his unexpected bond with one Arnold Schwarzenegger . From cigar-filled boat rides and chess matches to annual Christmas parties and charitable toy drives , their relationship extends well beyond the two other times they’ve been castmates after playing dueling Terminators. At this stage of his life, Luna even considers Schwarzenegger a father figure, having been raised in Austin, Texas, by his widowed single mother. Related Stories TV Fourth 'Terminal List' Show in the Works at Prime Video TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners Luna knew he was in rarefied air when he received an invitation to the Schwarzenegger family Christmas party in 2022, the first since the pandemic forced a two-year hiatus. Rather than the usual sprawling guest list, the gathering had been scaled down from 250 people to just 25. There, he rubbed elbows with Schwarzenegger’s son-in-law, Chris Pratt . The Terminal List , Pratt’s action-thriller series, hadn’t officially been renewed for a second season at that point, but the star-executive producer still had a role in mind for Luna, who would eventually play James Reece’s (Pratt) former SEAL teammate turned CIA operative, Freddy Strain. “I got to asking him about how The Terminal List was going, and he said, ‘If we’re blessed to get a second season, there’s a part that’s perfect for you,’” Luna tells THR during his lunch break on the Vancouver-based set of The Last of Us season three. “So that job started as a brotherly handshake in King Arnold’s court.” The domino effect didn’t stop there. While working on The Terminal List together, Luna caught the attention of director Marcos Siega, who had another casting idea up his sleeve. As an in-house director and executive producer on Dexter: Resurrection , Siega knew the second episode of the show’s second season would introduce “The Sleep-Eyed Stranger,” a nocturnal serial killer whose real name is Ray Ballard. So he gauged Luna’s interest on the set of Terminal List ‘s penultimate episode of season two, and he soon agreed to play his first villain away from Schwarzenegger. “Personally, I’m drawn to heroic characters. I always try to depict characters that my grandmothers would’ve been proud of,” Luna says. “So, up to this point, I’d only played bad guys for Arnold Schwarzenegger [in Dark Fate and FUBAR ].” Naturally, as Dexter’s (Michael C. Hall) latest problem to solve, “Sleepy” isn’t long for this world. But the experience did give Luna an opportunity to provide his Dexter -loving wife, Smaranda Luna, with the photo of all photos. “There’s a great photo of my girl [next to me as I’m Saran-wrapped on Dexter’s kill table]. She’s a big fan of the show, so she had me right where she wanted me,” Luna recalls mid-laugh. “I joked that she could’ve asked for anything in that moment, and I would’ve been powerless against her.” Luna, as Tommy Miller, is currently two-thirds of the way through filming The Last of Us ‘ third and final season. The series continues to move forward without its former leading man, Pedro Pascal, as well as video game franchise co-creator Neil Druckmann, who parted ways with co-creator and showrunner Craig Mazin between seasons . Luna says the spirit of both Pascal and Druckmann remains very much alive on set, with him, Mazin and co-stars Bella Ramsey and Kaitlyn Dever committed to honoring their previous collaborators. “Bella and I are the longest-tenured people on this set, so we’re carrying the DNA of the story, Neil’s intentions and his spirit forward. Craig loves the story that Neil has constructed, and he’s been a very stable steward who honors and maintains the source material,” Luna says. “We’re doing our absolute best to bring the most explosive, most heart-wrenching culmination. I just want to give the fans of the game and the fans of the show exactly what they deserve, which is, however morally ambiguous, a very explosive ending.” Below, in a conversation with THR , Luna also discusses spoiler details from his Terminal List and Dexter roles, elaborates on The Last of Us ‘ final season and shares his renewed hope of playing Robbie Reyes/ Ghost Rider again. *** So The Terminal List season two was last year, Dexter: Resurrection kicked off this year and it’s been The Last of Us season three ever since? Correct. The Terminal List took us to South Africa, Toronto and Morocco. We wrapped in November of ‘25. Then my contribution to Dexter was shot this past spring over a couple months. And now I ‘m here in Vancouver shooting season three of The Last of Us . I’ve been watching Dexter since day one, and I still can’t quite figure out why I root for this serial killer as much as I do. Have you come up with the answer yet? My wife, Smaranda, has also been a huge fan of the show since its inception. She got me into a few of the seasons. It might be because we’re in his head. We spend so much time with him in his head, and we feel close to him. He’s behind enemy lines of our own morality and psyche. He’s able to step over that line and infiltrate in that way. So he’s become much closer to us than we would ordinarily allow someone like that. Of course, Michael C. [Hall] is such an inviting presence. He’s a great actor, and I’m sure that has something to do with it. L-R: Gabriel Luna as Ray Ballard / Sleepy-Eyed Stranger and Michael C. Hall as Dexter Morgan in Dexter: Resurrection, episode 3, season 2, streaming on Paramount+, 2026. Matt Infante/Paramount+ You’ve never struck me as someone who could be described as “sleepy-eyed.” What was your reaction to the description of The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger on first read? Personally, I’m drawn to heroic characters. I always try to depict characters that my grandmothers would’ve been proud of, but there’ve been a few exceptions to the rule. Of course, I played a Terminator for Arnold in Terminator: Dark Fate , and then I played a villain again for Arnold on Fubar . So, up to this point, I’d only played bad guys for Arnold Schwarzenegger. The character of The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger was offered to me by Marcos Siega, who was one of our directors on The Terminal List. The Terminal List character’s efficiency and focus and dedication to his system probably put me in his mind when they were trying to cast Dexter . I love Marcos, and he brags now that he’s the only guy to kill me twice. He directed the episode of Terminal List where Freddy Strain meets his heroic end. And then, of course Dexter always gets his at some point. But when I first read the character, I just responded to how exact he was and how he liked to prolong the sensation and the torture of his victims — to the point where he’s their reprieve from the madness he’s induced upon them. Yeah, the rearranging of household items just to drive people crazy is especially cruel. He was introduced in episode two with a highly effective Nine Inch Nails needle drop, “The Day the World Went Away.” We also saw how he uses online real estate listings to get the lay of the land before breaking into homes and observing his future victims as they sleep. The Sleepy-Eyed Stranger really illustrates the potential downside of having our homes listed on sites like Zillow, doesn’t he? Yeah, when we bought our house in L.A., we just drove around. It was better for us to do it the more personal, old-school way. So it’s an interesting tool he uses. He probably targets new homeowners. They haven’t yet got their full security up and running, if he’s able to do these weekly home invasions and all of this foundational work for what is, in his mind, their ultimate release and then his release as well. He’d have to find very specific requirements for him to be able to achieve this. But I quickly put all the logic away because if I was going to try to break it down that way, I would’ve shaved my face for the character. I would’ve worn a hair net. I would’ve tried, as much as I possibly could, not to leave any DNA around the scene. But Michael C. was the same. He had his moments where he was like, “I don’t know, but it’s a [show]. Let’s just do it.” He lives a solitary life and believes relationships do more harm than good. How did you wrap your head around his philosophy that he’s doing his victims and their surviving loved ones a favor by ending their relationships? It’s tragic. ( Luna is interrupted by a Last of Us assistant with an update on the upcoming scene’s blocking. He then politely asks for his guitar to be retrieved from set. ) Sorry, we’re coming back from lunch. I constructed this tragic backstory that he’s in a bit of arrested development. He falls into that category of “hurt people hurt people” and probably underwent a lot of abuse by people who were supposed to be close to him and protect him. Then it just spiraled out of control into this new philosophy that any type of human interaction or connection is just a hindrance or an anchor or this curse and poison to one’s life, and that he’s the one to excise that poison. As we were working it out, it manifested through these tempestuous, childlike knee-jerk reactions. He doesn’t really talk to a lot of people or see a lot of people, so he’s lacking when it comes to understanding social contracts and connecting with people. When Dexter is trying to set him up and says, “You have a good share for Prater,” he quickly snaps back, “I know I have a good share.” It’s almost like a child who’s fighting with a step-sibling or something. But in my mind, it’s all rooted in childhood, and that’s how it manifests in his adult life. [ Writer’s Note: That petulant quality recurs when Dexter slices his cheek for his blood slide trophy. Instead of taking the pain like a tough guy, he reacts like a child. ] L-R: Michael C. Hall as Dexter Morgan and Gabriel Luna as Ray Ballard in Dexter: Resurrection, episode 3, season 2, streaming on Paramount+, 2026. Matt Infante/Paramount+ How would you describe the experience of being Saran-wrapped to Dexter’s kill table? Oh man. They told me that I’m probably in the upper tier of people who have spent the most time in the Saran wrap. I may have set a record somewhere along the line, I was told, partially because there’s a whole scene of dialogue between Uma Thurman and Michael C. before Dexter and Sleepy get into their little tête-à-tête and he plunges his knife into his sternum. But it did feel exciting. It’s an iconic scenario and set. They give you modesty undergarments because you’re in your birthday suit on that slab. They Velcro you in, and then they use a staple gun to get it tight. So I was up there for a while, and I guess I’m impressed by my endurance in staying on the table. They feed you snacks and bring you a little sippy cup with a straw in it just so you’re not too peckish or dehydrated up there. There’s a great photo of my girl [next to me as I’m Saran-wrapped on Dexter’s kill table]. Like I said, she’s a big fan of the show, so she had me right where she wanted me. I joked that she could’ve asked for anything in that moment, and I would’ve been powerless against her. The last time we spoke, you talked about attending the Schwarzenegger family’s Christmas party in 2022. Arnold is also the father-in-law of The Terminal List star Chris Pratt. So did Chris cast you on The Terminal List in between Christmas carols at the Schwarzenegger estate? ( Laughs .) That’s exactly what happened, although Arnold doesn’t really have Christmas carols. He always has a mariachi band at his parties, which I’ve always loved. So this was the first Christmas dinner, post-COVID, [in 2022]. In prior years, he had big 250-person parties with whole petting zoos. He had a sanctuary of rescued wild animals, and they would bring animals over. All of the usual suspects were there: Dolph [Lundgren], Danny DeVito, Sly [Stallone[] and everybody. But this time, we showed up for Christmas dinner together, and there were only 25 people there. I was really honored to be in that small family group. Katherine [Schwarzenegger] and Chris were sitting at our table, along with Conyers [Davis], Arnold’s chief of staff, and his wife Elizabeth. Chris and I were just talking about life, football, music and where we come from, specifically my background in Texas. Then I got to asking him about how The Terminal List was going, and he said, “If we’re blessed to get a second season, there’s a part that’s perfect for you.” That part, of course, was Freddy Strain. This was in 2022, and a lot of things happened from then until now. Between his busy schedule and the strike, there were numerous postponements to the second season getting going. But when it did get going, it happened in a perfect window right after I finished Devil in Disguise . I was already in Toronto, and I took a two-month break for The Last of Us press tour. Then I was back to work in Toronto on The Terminal List . So that job started as a brotherly handshake in King Arnold’s court. Chris Pratt (James Reece), Gabriel Luna (Freddy Strain) in The Terminal List Season 2 Justin Lubin/Prime Freddy is introduced as an old teammate of James Reece who now works for the CIA. More importantly, he’s a family man who represents everything James used to be. I figured your character was safe just because the story needed that juxtaposition, but as soon as Freddy’s previously unseen family was shown on a video call, I knew the worst was about to happen. Was Freddy’s death difficult for you to stomach? You hit the nail on the head. I just saw a funny internet video where the characters who always get taken out in war films are the ones who are busy talking about their girl’s picture in their wallet or their kids back home. It’s a departure from what was in the novel, and the sniper duel is much more exciting in the way it’s structured. It’s really a beautiful tribute to the character and his ability. He’s outmanned and outgunned, and he still puts up a hell of a fight. That day was very special, and a lot of heart and emotion was put into it. Jared Shaw wrote it. He’s a former team guy, a former Navy SEAL from SEAL Team 4, and he was one of my best friends on the shoot. In many ways, he’s the inspiration for Freddy Strain. I remember him being there with me right before those moments, just supporting me and encouraging me and giving me both a literal and figurative pat on the back when it went well and everything felt right. You can see me in my head getting tuned up at one point, and he just placed his hand on my back and said, “You’re doing beautiful, man. You got this.” It was all about honoring the fallen in that episode and the early scenes of the finale. That’s really the main focus and the main drive for all of it. We don’t want to do dishonor to the men and women who serve, specifically the frogmen who we’re trying to represent. [Freddy’s death] was the last day of the shoot, the absolute last day in Morocco, and it couldn’t have been spent better. Moving over to The Last of Us , Craig Mazin went solo between seasons two and three, with co-creator Neil Druckmann no longer actively involved in the show. Is everything business as usual as far as you’re concerned? Yeah, as far as it goes for me, I have a job to do. Bella and I are the longest-tenured people on this set, so we’re carrying the DNA of the story, Neil’s intentions and his spirit forward. Craig loves the story that Neil has constructed, and he’s been a very stable steward who honors and maintains the source material. Craig loves his work, however hard it is. Every letter of every word of every script is written by Craig Mazin, so we just have a lot of well-earned belief and trust in him. And so we carry on. We’re doing our absolute best to bring the most explosive, most heart-wrenching culmination to what has been a really beautiful five years in my life. I just want to give the fans of the game and the fans of the show exactly what they deserve, which is, however morally ambiguous, a very explosive ending. It’s what the piece deserves, and I’m excited to see everyone’s reaction. It’s been massive, man. We’ve been going since last March, and we probably won’t end until March, so it’ll be a lot of time and effort dedicated to what has always been a one-of-a-kind story. Everyone is at the top of their game. So we’re thankful for Craig, and I’m thankful for Bella and Kaitlyn [Dever]. They’re shouldering the massive weight of all this on their very slight shoulders, and I try my best, as Uncle Tommy, to offer what I can in support. (L-R) Gabriel Luna and Pedro Pascal attend The Mandalorian and Grogu Los Angeles World Premiere in Los Angeles, California on May 14, 2026. Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images Is Pedro Pascal’s absence still felt on set? Yeah, the spirit of Joel runs through everything. Pedro committed such an extraordinary performance to the screen, and you know the audience is certainly holding that flame for him. All the characters are too. In every action, in every life Tommy takes and in every round fired, there is that longing for his brother. I know Bella feels the same way about Ellie and the character’s grief. So, in the world of the show and in our memories of the great time we spent working together, we just carry him with us. But I always say Bella Ramsey is a great general, and we’re in great hands with them at the helm. Were you disappointed that you weren’t around for Joel’s death, as Tommy was in the games? It was actually my suggestion. In the first season, I had discussed the idea with Craig and Neil. To have such a capable character walk in and be so quickly incapacitated — and to be helpless while these people take his brother from him — just didn’t sit right. It was always something in the game that I questioned. Tommy would’ve had the situational awareness not to utter his brother’s name to strangers, which he does in the game. He’s the one who reveals Joel’s identity. So I always lobbied and pitched the idea, What if Tommy isn’t there? I remember seeing Craig clock the idea, and I’d keep inquiring about it. Then, once he got into the writer’s room for season two with Neil and [writer] Halley [Gross], Craig sent me a long, long text about what it would be now. And instead of helplessly being there as Joel is murdered, Tommy is back in Jackson fending off the horde of monsters as they breached the gates. He wrote literally everything you see on the screen in this big, long text. I was so excited and tortured and tormented for the following months to years, having to keep that all under my hat. I couldn’t be happier with the execution. It was truly an all-time episode. You have both that massive battle and then the departure of the heart of the show. There was a lot of recovery and resolution of that over the course of the remainder of the season. We then left the audience on a bit of a cliffhanger, but now we really get to finish the story. We get to give them the resolution that they all desire and that we desire as the people making it. We’re now moving toward the home stretch here, and everyone is going to be very excited and very pleased. Bella Ramsey as Ellie and Gabriel Luna as Tommy on The Last of Us season two. Liane Hentscher/HBO Danny Ramirez, as Manny, was present for Joel’s death and taunted his dead body. Oddly enough, Danny gave up his role in season three to work with Pedro again in Todd Haynes’ next movie, De Noche . You also got to work with Danny on his soccer movie? Yes, I did on Baton . It’s a fantastic script that he wrote based on his own true experience. He came to me and said, “I want you to be in the movie.” And I was like, “I love you, brother. Whatever you want.” And he was like, “I want you to play my dad.” And I was like, “You know what? Eff you. I take offense to that. I’m only [9] years older than you.” And he was like, “No, no, no. It’s all in flashbacks.” And I was like, “Okay, I’ll do it.” He’s just an incredible kid and a great creative spirit. He’s so ambitious, so talented and an incredible athlete. He’s a phenomenal soccer player, and he brings all that to the table. We went up to Miami for a week, and I shot out all my stuff for him, so I can’t wait to see it. The cast is excellent and primarily Latino. That’s a much-needed addition to the landscape of cinema at the moment. It tends to be a pretty fruitful one if people trust the talent in this community and allow them to bring their dreams to fruition. There’s a Ghost Rider movie in the works, and what’s good for one Ghost Rider is good for all Ghost Riders. Are you still keeping the flame burning a little bit? Years ago, my stock answer to this question was that I was so proud of what we did with Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and with Robbie Reyes that to continue it would only give me the potential or the opportunity to tarnish it. But as the multiverse started to take shape within the films and the questions started to be asked at a higher clip, I eventually had to pivot in my stance. I now think that there is potential, and I’m absolutely open to it. The character is much younger in the books, but if there’s a world where you age him up a little bit and time passes, then the evolution and the maturity of the character is allowed to happen, even though he’s a dead man. So there is a world where it makes sense, even if it’s just a bit of a cameo to step in and to honor that character and all the fans who’ve really held the torch for ten years now. I just did a 10-year anniversary thing at L.A. Comic-Con in celebration of the character, and it’s really, really awesome to see how many people still love Robbie and are still calling for that. So I’ve changed my stance. I’m absolutely open to it if I have the time and they have the story. I’m totally willing. There’s also an upcoming Marvel series called Zodiac , which many believe is connected to Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. So there’s more than a glimmer of hope that Robbie could ride again. Oh man, I’m ready. That was a great milestone in my life and my career. I’ve maintained my health and my agility. Mason Novick, whose credits include Juno and Jennifer’s Body , is producing alongside industry vet Ted Field, known for movies including Cocktail , Three Men and a Baby and Revenge of the Nerds and who previously helped revive horror franchises including The Amityville Horror and The Texas Chainsaw Massacre . Related Stories Casting Johnny Knoxville Joins 'Mt. Mystic' Comedy Series News Restored 'Jackass' Episodes Return To Paramount+ In Original Versions Rodger May will serve as executive producer through MayDay Movie Productions, alongside Christopher W. Fox, whose father, Tom Fox, produced the franchise’s previous five installments. The plan is to shoot next spring; producers say that private investment is behind the movie. Watch on Deadline Set in 1984, this new film is a direct sequel to Dan O’Bannon’s 1985 horror film The Return of the Living Dead , and is described as “expanding the mythology of the original while preserving its signature blend of punk rock, dark comedy and outrageous zombie horror.” The production will rely entirely on practical creature effects, with special makeup effects guru Tony Gardner ( Chucky , Zombieland , Rise of the Planet of the Apes ) overseeing the film’s zombie creations. The filmmakers have committed to a no-CGI approach, seeking to recapture the handcrafted horror that helped define the original. The original became a cult hit, introducing audiences to brain-hungry zombies and a mix of punk music and black comedy. The film spawned multiple sequels. The first film told the story of how a warehouse owner, accompanied by his two employees, mortician friend and a group of teenage punks, deal with the accidental release of a horde of unkillable, brain-hungry zombies onto an unsuspecting town. “I love — not like, love — Wolsh’s script,” said Field. “His commitment to absolutely no CGI and all practical effects is going to make this movie truly special for the fans.” “We chose to make this film independently because, while it’s a harder, longer road, I didn’t want the wrong cooks in the kitchen,” said Wolsh. “I’m ecstatic about our team, our cast and the vision we’re bringing to life: a hard-R, blood-soaked dark comedy driven entirely by practical effects. We want this film to be both a love letter to the original and a crowd-pleaser for a whole new generation of horror fans.” The Return of the Living Dead has its roots in a novel by John Russo, simply titled Return of the Living Dead , which served as a follow-up to Night of the Living Dead (1968) which Russo co-scribed with horror icon George A. Romero. When Russo and Romero went their separate ways after Night of the Living Dead , Russo retained rights to any titles featuring Living Dead while Romero was free to create his own series of sequels, beginning with Dawn of the Dead (1978). Over the years, Wolsh acquired rights to make another The Return of the Living Dead movie. An adjacent project of the same name was in the works in recent years with Wolsh and actor Devon Sawa attached. We’re told the project shot in part and was designed more as a short/teaser/proof of concept. Knoxville is repped by CAA and Sloane, Offer. title: Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done
full_text: Nov 18, 2026 8:15am PT Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done By Jazz Tangcay Plus Icon Jazz Tangcay Artisans Editor @jazzt Latest Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done 2 hours ago Venus and Serena Williams Set to Launch Season 2 of ‘Stockton Street’ Podcast on Dear Media (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago ‘The Odyssey’ Cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema Breaks Down Filming Climactic Thunderstorm Scene in Imax 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source After a weeklong run of screening Christopher Nolan ‘s “ The Odyssey ,” Universal saved the best for last, bringing out Steven Spielberg to moderate a one-on-one Q&A. As the film ended and the house lights went up, the pair walked out to a standing ovation from an audience of about 600 guild members and voters who had come out to see the film — many on repeat viewings. Before Spielberg had a moment to praise Nolan for the $1.8 billion blockbuster, it was Nolan who stepped in and humbly told Spielberg, “I just have to take a minute, because I’ve known you a long time, but I’ve never done a Q&A with you. When I was a younger man and a dear boy watching your movies, I don’t think I ever really envisioned this moment where you would be asking questions about my film.” Related Stories Skydance Reorgs TV and Streaming Distribution Leadership Team Post-Merger, Eight Execs to Exit Skydance Sports Chief Gives Top Roles to Jeff Gerttula, Craig Barry Spielberg told Nolan he had seen the film in Imax and called it “a showstopper.” When asked why now, and why he had chosen to adapt Homer’s poem, Nolan answered, “I always find it hard to figure out what to do next. Probably one of the reasons, if it’s been unpredictable, as you say, it’s because it’s always a surprise to me as well. I do one project at a time. I’m not very good at developing multiple things at the same time, so I finish one film and then I look for what might be next.” He continued, “What hadn’t really been done in the modern era was Greek mythology and I think the reason is because it hadn’t been done definitively. Part of the reason was because of the mythological elements; the visual effects techniques weren’t really available in the 1930s or the 1950s. When the great eras of the classical world, the world of antiquity, was big in Hollywood. ‘The Odyssey’ hadn’t been done on this scale with this movie budget, with the resources of modern technology: shooting on Imax, using visual effects and all the rest.” Nolan also talked about building his cast and choosing Matt Damon to play Odysseus. “This is one of the greatest things Matt has ever done as an actor,” Spielberg said. Nolan said, “Matt occurred to me right away because I’ve done two films with him in small parts. So I know from my own experience on the floor how incredible he is as an actor and how great he is to work with. How he’s just an incredible team member. He’s an incredible creative force. He’s not just thinking about his own part. He’s thinking about the whole narrative, which is a great asset. But also, he’s grown up on camera. You know, from that kid in ‘Saving Private Ryan.’ He has this ability to open up a story and take us on a journey, in empathetic terms; that’s incredibly powerful.” Spielberg took a moment to tell Nolan that one of his favorite scenes in the film featured Samantha Morton as the witchy goddess Circe, and he wanted to know how Nolan pulled it off. Spielberg said, “She was wonderful … That’s one of my favorite scenes in the whole movie, where they all turn into pigs.” Nolan explained he didn’t want to shoot in front of a green screen or use tracking markers. “I wanted to be able to define the process.” He said he watched transformation movies such as “An American Werewolf in London” and even Neil Jordan’s “A Company of Wolves” for inspiration. He revealed it was a collaboration with both the visual effects and special effects departments as they navigated the challenge. “They came up with these heads that have a skull underneath that’s fractured, but it’s held together with magnets and then it’s covered in a particular type of silicone skin that looked exactly wonderfully real, but was very flexible. So we built these heads of the guys, and each take, she could go around the table and do whatever she wanted and manipulate these guys however she wanted in the most horrible ways.” “The Odyssey” opened in July to a $264.1 million global debut, the biggest of Nolan’s career. It has since crossed $1.8 billion, becoming his highest-grossing film. Universal and Nolan’s team are continuing to focus on the format. title: Hudson Williams and His Hairstylist Aika Flores Really Are That Close
full_text: × Skip to main content Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty’s Next Billion-Dollar Mogul close Hudson Williams with groomer Aika Flores photographed by Jake Chessum on Oct. 30 at PMC Studios in New York City. Styling by Anastasia Walker. On Williams: Tom Ford sweater, scarf, pants; Bulgari jewelry. On Flores: Viviano shirt, pants, tee; Flores’ jewelry; Public School hat. Photographed by Jake Chessum; Groomer: Aika Flores It was early December 2025 when actor Hudson Williams met celebrity groomer Aika Flores . His queer Canadian hockey series, Heated Rivalry , had been out for just over a week, but the show was already catching fire on social media and at workplace water coolers. The pair met when Flores was hired by her close friend to do grooming for a cover shoot with Timid Magazine . “[My friend and editor-in-chief] Henry was telling me, ‘It’s this show that’s on the second episode. I think it’s going to get big. People are already talking about it. He’s hot,’” Flores tells The Hollywood Reporter about the pitch on Williams. Related Stories THR Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty's Next Billion-Dollar Mogul General News 'Heated Rivalry' Star Connor Storrie, 'Obsession' Ingenue Inde Navarette and 'Backrooms' Filmmaker Kane Parsons Set as BAFTA U.S. Breakouts Flash forward 11 months, and she and Williams are sprawled out on a couch in the green room of THR’s New York photo studio. It’s a rare break in filming for Williams, who’s knee deep in filming the second season of Heated Rivalry . As predicted, the show blew up, became a cultural phenomenon and launched the 25-year-old Canadian actor into an overnight sensation and a certified heartthrob. It didn’t take long for Williams’ authentic appreciation for skincare to land him a brand ambassadorship with his favorite Korean skincare company Skin 1004. But Williams has had virtually no time over the last year between returning to the hockey romance series, his latest show AMC+’s Yaga and a slew of other roles he’s booked in the wake of his breakout. It’s been intense. And Flores has been by his side the entire time. “The vibes were so good,” says Williams of their first meeting. “I was so tired that day, but we were already getting into our early lives, where we grew up.” That one-day booking for a U.S. press day turned into jetsetting around the world together this past year for media appearances and red carpets. “[His team] wanted to see first if we got along, and then they booked [me for the rest of the tour] while we were doing the shoot,” Flores says. “She was grounding, chill, funny,” says Williams. “Sometimes over-talkative people are just a little bit much in the morning, especially when [there are] always late nights. Those people that always have energy. I’m like, whoa, whoa, whoa.” On Williams: Zegna shirt; Bulgari jewelry. On Flores: Balenciaga jacket; Viviano jacket; her own jewelry; Public School Hat. Photographed by Jake Chessum Flores reminds Williams that he’s pretty high energy — except when he’s in her chair getting ready. “Quiet time,” he says. This is in high contrast to only minutes earlier, when the pair were joking around shooting video content: Williams taking a stab at being the one to pamper Flores for a change, Flores attempting to get the actor ready as he jumped out of the chair and dodge her hands. The horseplay on set might have one assume that they are close friends. “We’re like family now,” Flores says. Williams describes how he’s become “Uncle Hudson” to Flores’ son. “He made me brush his teeth,” he says, fondly. Uncle Hudson has been known to prep for bedtime stories with the same dedication he applies to scenes, using voices for the characters, something Flores jokes that she and her wife don’t even do. “I was sort of nervous, I had to play Santa,” Williams says. “I was like, ‘I hope he’s not judging me.’” That almost familial closeness helped Williams through a whirlwind year. After Heated Rivalry finished airing around Christmas 2025, his schedule exploded with late-night tapings, Golden Globes presenting, Olympic torch-bearing, Milan runway walking and more life-changing experiences. Through it all, Flores, along with his CAA branding agent Leilani Houston and stylist Anastasia Walker, have been by his side. “It’s been great because honestly. We call our group chats the quad squad,” Williams says. “Yesterday we hung out until 3 a.m., after a day where we were up in the morning, and it was a 12-hour shooting day because we just love each other so much,” Williams adds. “We all take care of each other. It’s kind of like a maternal energy towards everyone. It feels like we’re sisters braiding each other’s hair or something — with alcohol.” Williams leans on the quad when online commentary gets intense. “A lot of times social media is just inherently mean, and so everyone gets shot at online,” he continues. “We always have each other, and there’s a feeling that since we’re always aligned and we always have this group that we will always be together.” Flores says they often laugh the hate off because it’s the only way to go about it. “It’s outrageous, so it’s so funny,” Williams says. “It’s like speculation or they make it up,” adds Flores. “When we come across it, we’re like, ‘Oh my God, did you know that I got shot yesterday? Did you know that I’m actually really problematic, I guess?’ We just laugh because it’s so stupid,” she continues. “That’s what’s nice, is having each other,” adds Williams. On Williams: Tom Ford sweater, scarf, pants, shoes; Bulgari jewelry. On Flores: Viviano shirt, pants, tee, shoes; Flores’ jewelry; Public School hat. Photographed by Jake Chessum Even as Williams signature heartthrob hair has been a hit online, plenty of people have speculated that Flores is somehow forcing Williams into looks he doesn’t want. “I want my hair to be the same,” the actor clarifies. “It’s how he likes it, and I just elevate it, and then we bounce off ideas,” Flores adds. The pair also like to take risks, his daring Met Gala look of exaggerated cat eyes and sculpted wet hair landing on many best-of lists. “She popped off with the Met,” says Williams. “We like to have fun, and not take anything too serious. [We] just try things, be bold.” Heated Rivalry is taking up much of his time lately, rejoining his co-star Connor Storrie to film the show’s highly anticipated next season in Toronto. “It’s going good, but it’s sad,” Williams says, referencing the material they’ll be tackling in the next season. It’s based on author Rachel Reid’s follow-up The Long Game , which show creator Jacob Tierney has previously referred to as “Sex Scenes From A Marriage .” There’s not much Williams can say about what they’re getting up to on the set, but he did note that the return made him a little nervous. “Leading up to [filming], I was getting kind of scared of how it’d feel, but it’s the same crew. Jacob does a really good job of making it feel just as small and intimate,” he says. “Even the joining cast, they immediately picked up on the vibe and were so sweet. We’re all supportive of each other. It’s just a really fun time. Still feels tiny, [it’s] just crazy,” adds Williams. “It’s just a bigger family now.” For The Hollywood Reporter ‘s 10th Beauty Issue, Williams and Flores talked about “evil” hair, that time he got scolded by a security guard (and the internet) for lighting a smoke on the streets of Milan, and why in times of exhaustion, Williams likes to “take a nap on Aika.” Photographed by Jake Chessum *** What’s been your favorite look? FLORES I think my favorite look has to be the Met [Gala]. WILLIAMS She popped off with the Met. FLORES It was so collaborative between me and [stylist] Anastasia that for, I feel like months, we were planning it. As soon as [Hudson] got invited, we were [planning]. We knew from the beginning we weren’t going to do a black suit. That’s just not his personality, [or any] of our personalities. WILLIAMS We like to have fun, and not take anything too serious. [We] just try to take risks and try things, be bold. That was my favorite too, as far as [it being] fun and getting the whole team to be working together so cohesively. I do like how nice I looked at the Oscars. As far as my face and hair. It’s one of my favorites just because my hair was wet looking. My skin was great. You elevated my skin. I liked the hair you did when I was going to the Armani show. FLORES Oh, the cigarette that he got in trouble for. WILLIAMS I wasn’t even trying to smoke that in the street, but I was like, “Will I have time to smoke it there?” I think it was Lei Lei, who was like, “I don’t think you have time.” So I asked, “Should I just smoke it while I’m walking?” But I felt like with the suit, how we worked with Armani to make that. Then how you worked with my hair, I thought that was cool. Is there a recent look you’ve loved? FLORES The Yaga premiere at TIFF, where his hair was like… He looked evil. WILLIAMS That was fun too. What look have you been trying lately? FLORES We’ve been toying a lot with wet hair because it’s cool. WILLIAMS I like wet hair. What do you like most about working with one another? WILLIAMS My favorite thing is — we just did a shoot yesterday for something I can’t say — but I got really tired in the middle of the shoot. It was a long shoot, and I had to do a bunch of stuff. I just took a nap on Aika, and that’s always fun. Whenever I have these big moments, I can just literally grab onto her and fall asleep. We’re always giggling and laughing and not taking it too seriously, which is fun. I feel like we always find something to laugh at. The vibes never go left. I feel like we’re very respectful of each other’s moods. FLORES My favorite, and I think this goes to just you being a person, is he can’t remember months or dates or anything that happened. But as soon as he sits in the chair, he remembers our last conversation, what we talked about last time. Obviously, we don’t really do small talk anymore, but we can appreciate silence together. We can just chill together. I don’t feel like I’m performing when I’m working with you. Is there a look you’ve been dying to try? WILLIAMS My hair is going to change for parts, so there’s definitely other styles I want to try. For one of these roles, I want to cut it into a crop sort of fringey thing, for a future part. FLORES He never told me this. WILLIAMS I have another thing that I might do where I’d have long ass hair, and if I had it, if it was real long hair, not a wig, learning how to style that would be fun. What’s a beauty trend you want to see get popular next year? WILLIAMS I’ve been putting barrettes [in my hair]. When I wear a hat, sometimes my hair wings out and sticks out like crazy, so I have little chrome heart and star barrettes. I put my little star clips in my hair. The ones for meant for five-year-old girls. I think men should get on the barrettes [trend] because they’re so cute. FLORES I second that. That’s dope. A version of this story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: ‘American Idol’ Gets Rid Of Hollywood Week In Favor Of More Live Shows As ABC Music Competition Moves To Georgia: “Major Changes Coming”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Vin Diesel To Star In Action Pic 'Burial Hill'; Amazon Closing Big Deal Read the full story By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter YouTube Hits Back At Rivals With New Slate Featuring Rising Creators, Established Stars & Hot New Directors ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Finale Will Go Live Across The Country For The First Time Skydance Cable Shakeup: Betsy Sanner Ayala, Jason Sarlanis, Tina Perry & Michael Ouweleen To Oversee Programming; Howard Lee Exiting View All November 18, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source American Idol: Lionel Richie, Ryan Seacrest, Carrie Underwood, and Luke Bryan Eric McCandless/Disney EXCLUSIVE : When Gladys Knight sang “Midnight Train to Georgia” on the season six finale of American Idol , backed by Ben Stiller, Jack Black and Robert Downey Jr., nobody thought that 20 years later the team behind the show would be taking her lyrics so literally. L.A. proved too much for the show, it seems, as the ABC music competition takes its live shows to the suburbs of Atlanta for the first time in its 25-year history. Deadline revealed in September that the Ryan Seacrest-hosted show would be relocating, but it is only one of a number of changes to the show as it heads into Season 25 (or Season 10 on ABC). Related Stories News ‘American Idol’ Moving Production To Georgia As ABC Series Becomes Latest To Leave California News ABC’s ‘American Idol’ Introduces Live Social Voting, Becomes First Reality Competition To Take The Leap The other major change to Idol is that there is a surprising new path to America’s Vote as the show eschews Hollywood Week for the first time. Watch on Deadline Contestants will no longer be heading to Hollywood (or Nashville, as it was last season), but instead judges Luke Bryan, Lionel Richie and Carrie Underwood will award 25 Golden Tickets, sending hopefuls straight to Hawaii. “This is a major departure, major changes coming,” American Idol showrunner Megan Michaels Wolflick told Deadline ahead of its return on Monday, February 8, 2027. By cutting out Hollywood Week, American Idol can get to the live shows quicker. The show will kick off with three audition episodes, followed by two shows in Hawaii before going live. “The auditions and the live shows are the bread and butter for this show and the process of a Hollywood Week is really a culling process that we were televising,” Michaels Wolflick added. “Going to America’s Vote is what this show is about. Hollywood was a metaphor.” The move essentially allows viewers to vote on their favorites earlier. It coincides with the 25th anniversary, hopefully giving it a Survivor 50 -style celebration. Megan Michaels Wolflick Fremantle Michaels Wolflick is known for regularly freshening up the format over the years, for instance, becoming the first major competition show to introduce social voting last season. “It keeps people on their toes,” she said. “We’re still keeping the cornerstones of the house, but we are just remodeling a room. The promise is still there but it’s really nice to switch it up and we’re keeping the integrity and the dream of the show.” The top 25 from the auditions will be sent straight to the Disney resort Aulani in Ko Olina, Hawaii to perform. They will also be joined by one more singer, who can score America’s Golden Ticket. Three hopefuls who did not receive one of the tickets from the judges will be featured during the Country Music Awards and on social media with fans voting on social media – Facebook, Instagram and TikTok – as to who will get the spot. Votes will be cast between November 18 and 25 with the winner being announced on ABC’s Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve. Michaels Wolflick said that last season’s social voting went well and she was excited to do it again. She noted that people on different platforms voted differently; unsurprisingly, Facebook voters were older. “The win for me was the growth across the season and I still feel there’s so much more ground to cover next year,” she added. American Idol has filmed its live shows in Los Angeles for the last 24 years but will spend eight weeks at Trillith Live, outside of Atlanta. “We’ve always been kind of looking at it because there’s been other shows that have moved over the past couple of years,” she said. “The thing about Idol is we have always traveled. We have filmed [auditions] in Georgia for many years. It didn’t feel that disruptive for us.” The move is bad news for Los Angeles, which saw 40% fewer unscripted TV shoot days in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year. Idol is following shows such as The Masked Singer , which moved to New Jersey, with other big competition shows such as The Voice and America’s Got Talent eyeing moves out of California as well. California’s tax credit does include large-scale competition shows but Deadline understands Idol wasn’t eligible, which means the move to Georgia, which offers up to a 30% tax credit for unscripted and reality television productions that spend at least $500,000 in the state, makes more financial sense. “Georgia wants to incentivize filming. Our state [California] does not,” she said. “We barely ever got outside the studio. We weren’t outside at the Hollywood Bowl. The dream of the show is to perform on an incredible stage with an incredible band with hair and makeup and wardrobe at the top tier level in the industry, and we can still provide that.” Soon after American Idol premiered on Fox in 2002, it started to see competition. There was USA Network’s Nashville Star , NBC’s Fame and CBS’ Rock Star. But in 2011, Fox and NBC took bigger swings to compete with the Fremantle and 19 Entertainment-produced show including U.S. versions of The X Factor and The Voice. The X Factor may well be back as a new iteration is in development at Fox . ABC also has new music competition series Who’s In The Band? launching in the summer, after Idol finishes its run. Michaels Wolflick said that as long as these shows aren’t going head-to-head, like they did back in the day, there’s room for more music on television. “It used to be more Hunger Games ,” she added. “I still have the Hunger Games mentality when making [ Idol ] in my own head. I really do. I’m always [thinking], ‘How can we change? How can we adapt? What can we do?’ I’m very competitive.” ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Turns Chaos & Crime Into Record-Shattering Launch Meet The New Pic’s Cast As Title & Release Date Are Unveiled ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Finale Will Go Live Across The Country For First Time ‘Return Of The Living Dead’ Sequel Disinterring With Johnny Knoxville Among Cast Read More About: 3 Comments

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Reviews: Critics Hail “The Most Impressive Video Game Ever”
full_text: × Skip to main content Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty’s Next Billion-Dollar Mogul close By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All November 18, 2026 7:36am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Rockstar Games Logo text After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally arriving. And the reviews? Pretty much as glowing as they could possibly be. Right out of the gate, the hotly anticipated Rockstar Games title has a 99 out of 100 score on Metacritic, tying with 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the review aggregator site’s highest-rated game. In fact, 100 percent of critics are recommending the game. Across dozens of reviews, the superlatives keep coming: “Masterpiece,” “magnum opus,” “revolutionary,” “unprecedented,” “breathtaking,” “jaw-dropping,” “astonishing.” Related Stories Business 'GTA 6' vs. Hollywood: Industry Braces for "Biggest Entertainment Launch in History" Business Don't Have 210 Spare GBs? 'GTA VI' Is Coming to Xbox Cloud Gaming (and the Xbox One) at Launch An IGN critic writes, “I regularly find myself in love with video games , but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.” While Eurogamer writes, “ GTA 6 is the most believable and unbelievable game of your lifetime.” Critics hail the story as a Bonnie and Clyde romance following two lovers, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, as they try to escape the criminal life in a fictional version of Florida. According to The Washington Post , which calls the game an “astonishing American epic,” the playscape is stuffed with a staggering 33,000 unique non-playable characters, reflecting the tens of thousands of people who were involved in the game’s writing, programming and acting. The game also includes 600,000 animations (versus 55,000 in GTA V ) and an incredible 1,500 songs. The main story takes roughly 70 hours to complete. Critics also praise the game as a sharp social satire, tackling everything from conspiracy theorists to wealth inequality to online influencers to the manosphere to men’s rights activists to AI tech. The environment is so sprawling, writes The Guardian , that “reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris.” GameSpot wrote the game is “a giant haystack full of needles that you’ll constantly find.” The New York Times heralds the romance at the heart of the game: “ GTA VI will steal your heart. The series matures beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups with a game about love, relationships and nurturing your partner. … Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterization of the two leads. Lucia and Jason’s relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between.” A PC Mag review drills down on game’s play mechanics: “Any screenshot will show you how many elements are packed into each frame. In motion, I was especially impressed by the moody shadows and striking lighting, impossibly perfect orange sunsets with a neon purple color palette that’s spiritually ’80s without being totally anachronistic. It’s proof of how realism and art direction don’t have to be mutually exclusive. And as for how it plays, the awkward driving and clunky shooting of past games are nowhere to be found here. Even punching people and dodging counterattacks, while basic, has smooth rhythm and flow … I never want to leave Grand Theft Auto VI because it knows the value of a vital vacation.” And CNET adds , “Like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned.” Did anybody say anything negative? That’s tougher to find, though The Guardian criticizes the game’s complex controls and unpredictability, writing, “This can be a frustrating game at times: unpredictable, laborious, unwieldy and, occasionally, unfair.” The $79.99 game is released Nov. 19 and expected to disrupt Hollywood’s entertainment releases , especially TV shows on streaming, though to what extent at this stage is difficult to measure. title: Amazon’s ‘One Night in Idaho’ Season 2 Reveals Premiere Date and Trailer (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty’s Next Billion-Dollar Mogul close By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All November 18, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bryan Kohberger appears at the Ada County Courthouse for his sentencing hearing on July 23, 2025 in Boise, Idaho. Kyle Green-Pool/Getty Images Amazon ‘s One Night in Idaho season two will be ready to consume — and to be consumed during — your Christmas break. The documentary series’ trio of new episodes , titled One Night in Idaho: Catching a Killer , will premiere on Prime Video on Dec. 28, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. We can also exclusively debut the Catching a Killer -season trailer (below). The first season, which was supposed to be limited to just that, was titled One Night in Idaho: The College Murders . The followup season was greenlit when Bryan Kohberger pled guilty to the gruesome murders of four University of Idaho students. Kohberger then attempted to walk back that plea, though it didn’t work: Kohberger is serving four consecutive life sentences at the Idaho Maximum Security Institution. Rot. Related Stories Business Disney and AWS Team Up to Create AI-Powered 'Star Wars' Robots TV Melania Trump Dismisses Media as "Noise" in Trailer for 'Melania' Doc Follow-Up In 2022, Kohberger brutally stabbed and killed Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Ethan Chapin and Xana Kernodle in their Moscow, Idaho rental home. The case spawned a pair of documentary projects, released eight days apart. Compare and contrast Prime Video’s One Night in Idaho: The College Murders and Peacock’s The Idaho Student Murders here . One Night in Idaho ‘s Catching a Killer volume features interviews with Brett Payne (lead detective on the case for Moscow, Idaho PD) and his wife Alyson, Darren Gilbertson (lead detective on the case for Idaho State Police), James Fry (chief of MPD at the time), Mitch Nunes (the first officer to arrive on the crime scene and discover the bodies), Shaine Gunderson (the third officer to arrive on the crime scene), Jon Habben (FBI agent in Los Angeles) who cracked the case using investigative genetic genealogy), Joe Traino (FBI agent in Pennsylvania who went undercover as a garbage man to obtain DNA evidence from the Kohberger family home) and Chris Paris (Pennsylvania State Police major who orchestrated the Kohberger raid and arrest). None of them have participated in previous documentaries, Amazon MGM Studios says. Many were under a gag order. Catching a Killer is directed by Matthew Galkin ( Murder in the Bayou ) and showrun by Katie A. King. It comes from Liz Garbus’ Story Syndicate, Paramount Television Studios, Amazon MGM Studios and James Patterson Entertainment; Fairhaven is also in the mix. Galkin and Garbus directed season one together. One Night in Idaho season two is executive produced by Galkin, Garbus, King, Dan Cogan, Jon Bardin, Joshua Levine, Tommy Coriale, Patterson, Bill Robinson and Patrick Santa. Watch the trailer: THR

title: ‘NAZA’ Team Sticking To Plan To Release Shattering Documentary On The Guardian Website Within Weeks — IDFA
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Vin Diesel To Star In Action Pic 'Burial Hill'; Amazon Closing Big Deal Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew IDFA Announces Winning Projects In Forum Section, With Prizes Worth More Than €30,000 IDA Awards Nominations: ‘Concrete Land’ Lands 6, With ‘To Hold A Mountain’ Close Behind; Elizabeth Holmes Doc In The Mix In ‘Ba’s Book,’ A Daughter Finds An Innovative Way To Unlock Her Father’s Extraordinary Memories — Trailer View All November 18, 2026 1:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Filmmaker Yuval Abraham (right) interviews a source in 'NAZA' The Guardian/JW Films The explosive documentary NAZA has become a worldwide box office sensation, earning $15 million to date. But if co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor had prevailed, it might have gone straight from its Venice Film Festival premiere to The Guardian website. “At first me and Rachel thought, let’s put it out online the next day,” Abraham explained as he appeared for a panel discussion about the film at International Documentary Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ). Their partners on the project convinced the filmmakers that a theatrical release should be part of how NAZA reached viewers. “It’s different audiences,” commented Fionnuala Jamison, managing director of sales agent-distributor mk2. “Online — it’s not necessarily everyone who’s going to be aware, who has that viewing habit to go watch something on The Guardian website or on YouTube, depending what people’s setups are. So, we felt it was something that could absolutely exist alongside for different audiences and at cinemas.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Documentary ‘NAZA’ Review: Israeli Military Accused Of Depraved Indifference To Palestinian Life, Using AI To Kill In Gaza – Venice Film Festival Documentary Explosive ‘NAZA’ Documentary, Attacked By Israeli Government, To Be Released In U.S. Theaters “Our North Star always has been how we’re going to get this film to people,” said Lindsay Poulton, head of documentaries at The Guardian, who produced the film alongside The Guardian’s Harry Davies and James Wilson of JW Films. “I think sitting in a cinema has been an important part of that. We’ve talked publicly as well about how the film is going to be available on our platform.” ‘NAZA’ panel L-R: Fionualla Jamison, James Wilson, Lindsay Poulton, moderator Neil Young. On screen is director Yuval Abraham. Courtesy of Coen Dijkstra Poulton and fellow panelists reiterated The Guardian intends to make the film available for free on its website in early December, although a specific date hasn’t been revealed. In the meantime, the documentary has played theatrically in 50 countries, and recorded a remarkable 1.6 million admissions . Abraham, part of the Oscar-winning quartet of directors of No Other Land , along with Szor, became a believer in the theatrical component. Appearing on the panel by remote from The Guardian offices in London, he said he realized, “The film being immediately accessible doesn’t necessarily translate to maximum impact. There is something to be gained from also doing this theatrical run.” ‘NAZA’ The Guardian/JW Films NAZA presents interviews with 24 anonymous members of Israeli intelligence and Israel Defense Forces personnel who describe how Israeli military leaders callously disregarded the potential loss of Palestinian civilian life as they pursued Hamas targets in Gaza. The whistleblowers claim this included deliberating striking Hamas militants at night in their homes with full knowledge those attacks would likely lead to the deaths of innocent women and children. The IDF has denied violating human rights standards and the Geneva Convention in its prosecution of the war. It has also denied an assertion in the film that the IDF used AI to select targets. The release of NAZA has triggered furor within Israel’s right-wing. The country’s Culture Minister, Miki Zohar, vowed to strip Abraham and Szor of their Israeli citizenship , a move later endorsed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu . Supporters of the Israeli government went so far as to quickly produce a counter documentary titled NAZA: The Real Story , mimicking the style of Abraham and Szor’s film by shooting it on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv. “There’s a film out there that’s very misleading. Obviously, it’s not a coincidence,” Abraham stated. “They call themselves NAZA . They’re trying to mislead people into thinking that they are the real NAZA film.” An IDFA audience attends the panel discussion about ‘NAZA’ Courtesy of Coen Dijkstra The director also told the audience at the DeLaMar Theater venue at IDFA that Israel’s military has released “this kind of guidebook for commanders giving them instructions or explaining to them how to speak with their soldiers about NAZA . So, it’s like for commanders in the Israeli Air Force and other officers sort of an explanation as to how you can deal with the claims that are raised in the film. And of course, they say what you’d expect them to say. And very high up it says that the purpose of this guidebook is to strengthen the soldier’s sense of the — they use this term ‘righteousness of the path, that what we are doing is right.’” Abraham said he didn’t view the existence of the guidebook or the counter documentary in wholly negative terms. “There’s also something positive about it which I think when you get people to be so defensive, when commanders feel a need to get this kind of guidebook to reassure their soldiers that the path is right and that the army is moral and immune from criticism and that they say NAZA [a Hebrew acronym meaning collateral damage], it’s not a bad term,” he noted. “There’s something also about being defensive, which is a reflection of the sense that you are scrutinized, the sense that you are under magnifying glass… They feel like they’re not only watching, they’re also being watched. They’re not only surveilling in a sense; they’re also being surveilled or looked at. And that’s good.” James Wilson, the Oscar-nominated producer ( Zone of Interest ) said the message of NAZA won’t be derailed by efforts at misinformation. “It’s about horror. It’s about mass murder that our society, the West, has been completely implicit in,” he insisted. “It couldn’t be about something more important and serious and sort of abyssal in its horror… It’s like an alarm. It’s a fucking alarm and we all have to bear witness to that as it’s happening.” Abraham concluded by saying, “People talk about films changing the world. I don’t think that a film can really do that, but I think films can definitely, as Jim [Wilson] was saying, they can definitely be part of a network, of a larger kind of energy that exists in the world, which is pushing for change, which is pushing for humanity and empathy.” ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Turns Chaos & Crime Into Record-Shattering Launch Meet The New Pic’s Cast As Title & Release Date Are Unveiled ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Finale Will Go Live Across The Country For First Time ‘Return Of The Living Dead’ Sequel Disinterring With Johnny Knoxville Among Cast Read More About: Comments

title: Jean-Pierre & Luc Dardenne Set For European Film Academy Lifetime Achievement Award
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Vin Diesel To Star In Action Pic 'Burial Hill'; Amazon Closing Big Deal Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Qatar’s Film Committee Head Hassan Al-Thawadi Teases 2nd Industry Days In Doha: “We Are moving From Vision To Execution” Jean-Pierre & Luc Dardenne Set For European Film Academy Lifetime Achievement Award Festival In Focus: Qatar Ramps Up International Film & TV Ambitions As Local Talent Shines View All November 18, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jean-Pierre & Luc Dardenne in 2012, and earlier on in their career Christine Plenus The European Film Academy will honor multi-award-winning Belgian directorial duo Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne with a Lifetime Achievement Award at its 39th European Film Awards in January 2027. Among the most internationally acclaimed filmmakers to emerge from Belgium and Europe, the brothers have left an indelible mark on European cinema history over the past four decades with their films exploring what it means to live in a society shaped by inequality, migration, and economic pressure. Born in Seraing, in the industrial region of Liège in Wallonia, the landscape and social realities of the region have been an important part of their cinema, providing both the setting and the social environment for many of their films. Related Stories News European Film Awards: 'Fatherland' & 'La Bola Negra' Top Nominations - Full List Of Films & Credits News Hiam Abbass To Receive Honorary European Film Academy Award Jean-Pierre Dardenne studied Dramatic Arts at the Institut des Arts de Diffusion in Brussels, where he was taught by the French playwright and director Armand Gatti. Watch on Deadline Through Gatti, the brothers became involved in filmmaking and started documenting the lives and experiences of people in their local community. Beginning their careers in the late 1970s, the Dardennes established themselves as documentary filmmakers through their production company Dérives, before moving onto fiction. The brothers made their first fiction feature film Falsch in 1987, adapted from a play by René Kalisky about the last surviving member of a Jewish family murdered during the Holocaust. They founded their production company Les Films du Fleuve in 1987. Its early production including The Promise (1996) gave a taste of the distinctive cinematic approach steeped in social issues and authenticity. Set in the industrial world of Liège, it followed Igor, a teenage mechanic’s apprentice whose father is involved in the exploitation of undocumented workers. Three years later, they would break out internationally with Rosetta , which won the brothers their first Cannes Palme d’Or. Starring now late actress Émilie Dequenne, the film revolved around a young woman struggling to find work and escape poverty. Dardennes have continued their relationship with Cannes and its main competition throughout their career. They won their second Palme d’Or in 2005 with The Child, starring Jérémie Renier as a young father who makes a devastating decision concerning his newborn son. In 2008, they won Best Screenplay for Lorna’s Silence , while The Kid With A Bike clinched the Grand Prix in 2011. In 2019, the Dardennes received the Cannes Best Director Award for Young Ahmed , while T ori and Lokita , a drama about two young migrants from Africa who have arrived in Belgium alone, received the the festival’s 75th Anniversary Prize in 2022. They were back at the festival in 2025 with Young Mothers , which received the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize. They also have a long relationship with European Film Academy. In 1997, Gigi, Monica… et Bianca won the European Film Award for Best Documentary, The Kid With A Bike received European Screenwriter Award, and Marion Cotillard clinched the European Film Award for Best Actress for her performance in their 2015 film Two Days, One Nigh t. “Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne have received some of the highest honours in European and international cinema,” the European Film Academy said in a statement announcing the honor. “Their work has been celebrated not only for its artistic achievement, but for its sustained engagement with questions of social inequality, migration, work, family and human dignity.” The brothers will receive their Lifetime Achievement Award at the European Awards Ceremony on January 17, 2027. ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Turns Chaos & Crime Into Record-Shattering Launch Meet The New Pic’s Cast As Title & Release Date Are Unveiled ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Finale Will Go Live Across The Country For First Time ‘Return Of The Living Dead’ Sequel Disinterring With Johnny Knoxville Among Cast Read More About: Comments

The drama, about Palestinian civilians trapped in a war zone, was to have played in the festival’s main competition aimed at first and second features and featuring a jury presided over by Marion Cotillard this year. “The Marrakech International Film Festival has been informed of the decision by Algerian production company Issaad Film Productions, the rights holder of Chronicles from The Siege … to withdraw the film from the Official Competition of the Festival’s 23rd edition,” Marrakech said in a statement. Related Stories Documentary Watermelon Pictures Condemns Killing Of 'American Doctor' Surgeon In Gaza Hospital Strike News 'NAZA' Becomes One Of The Most Watched Docs On Theatrical Release In 2026 The festival said the producers had originally confirmed the participation of Chronicles from the Siege , on June 1, and that Al-Khatib was not in agreement with the move to withdraw the film. Watch on Deadline “Abdallah Al-Khatib has strongly opposed this decision, both to the film’s producers and to the festival, and has made clear his wish for the film to remain in the Official Competition and be presented in Marrakech,” read the statement. “While the Festival acknowledges the director’s expressed wish to present his film in Marrakech, it is bound to respect the decision of the company holding the film’s rights and is therefore unable to retain it in the Festival’s programme,” continued the statement. Deadline has contacted Issaad Film Productions to clarify why it pulled film and is waiting for a response. There are long-simmering tensions between North African neighbors Algeria and Morocco, but this does not seem to have prompted the withdrawal. Deadline understands that the producers have instead cited the recent upgrading of diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israeli, which was unveiled in September. title: ‘Fjord’ DP Tudor Vladimir Panduru On Crafting Long Takes With Cristian Mungiu & Challenges Of Shooting In Remote Norway — ToruńCamerimage
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Vin Diesel To Star In Action Pic 'Burial Hill'; Amazon Closing Big Deal Read the full story By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Fjord’ DP Tudor Vladimir Panduru On Crafting Long Takes With Cristian Mungiu & Challenges Of Shooting In Remote Norway — ToruńCamerimage ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’ DP On Balancing Action Sequences With A Man’s “Spiritual Journey And Struggles Of Trying To Step Up As A Father” — ToruńCamerimage ‘Fatherland’ Takes Top Prize At ToruńCamerimage; ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Wins Audience Award View All November 18, 2026 3:52am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve in 'Fjord' Tudor Pandura/Neon Tudor Vladimir Panduru touched down at the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival in Poland last week where the cinematographer and frequent Cristian Mungiu collaborator reflected on how he crafted the visuals for the Romanian filmmaker’s Palme d’Or winning title Fjord . Panduru and Mungiu have been working together for more than a decade, working on titles such as Graduation and R.M.N. in addition to Fjord , and the DP notes that the long relationship means they have built a shorthand and “very specific visual language” together. Mungiu is known for his very long takes – notably shooting a 17-minute shot in R.M.N. – and Panduru says the pair have “perfected the way we work with these long takes.” Related Stories Festivals 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' DP On Balancing Action Sequences With A Man's "Spiritual Journey And Struggles Of Trying To Step Up As A Father" -- ToruńCamerimage Festivals 'Fatherland' Takes Top Prize At ToruńCamerimage; 'Wild Horse Nine' Wins Audience Award “We are comfortable with each other and we prepare a lot,” he says. “He brought me in on this project quite early on in pre-production and then we went to Norway to scout for locations.” Watch on Deadline Fjord , which is released by Neon in the U.S. and UK, follows a Norwegian woman (Renate Reinsve) and her devout Romanian husband (Sebastian Stan) who relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgement that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. “Cristian is a good observer, and he always wants to be truthful,” says Panduru. “And I follow that in that process of trying not to be judgemental in my approach as well. He continues: “From the point of the script, the story had some specificity. The fact that these two families were close to each other meant that we had to find a place or a geography that would tell that from the start, and that was the hardest thing throughout the process of the scout.” The team scouted from Bergen to Ålesund before finding neighbouring houses overlooking the water for the main characters. “It wasn’t so common to find two houses in such close vicinity because when we took the first photos and watched them, we were totally immersed in that universe. So, that’s a layer that wasn’t present in the script.” He admits that scheduling and the remote location made it a “hard production” at times. “It was tricky organizing everything and getting to the locations. You had to either take two ferries or a long road and a ferry, so we were quite stuck there. It was really remote.” A further challenge, he notes, was the fact that the story takes place across three seasons but was only shot in March and April. “When we scouted the third time in January, there was a lot of snow and we were hoping to have images with small characters in the snow, but it wasn’t like that. We had to use a bit of VFX on the way. The only evening shots that had a lot of snow were shot on the weekend because that’s when it happened. “Our first AD was the one who proposed we shoot when it was snowing at the weekend and we even convinced Sebastian to come with us for one of the shots. I think that was a really interesting part of doing Fjord , was the fact that the crew, who were from Romania, Norway, Finland, Sweden and all over, was really homogenous. We really were like a family, so we felt support from all sides.” Thanks to weather conditions, Panduru points out that one of the film’s more emotional scenes when Reinsve’s character’s children are taken into custody, was actually shot on the first day of the shoot “because we were supposed to shoot in the snow.” “Shooting such an intense scene for the first day was really interesting but, in a way, because we did that at the beginning, everybody understood what the film was about,” he says. Panduru says that one of the most challenging sequences was the “jump in the water”, a long take which sees the camera follow Reinsve’s character searching on the ground to jumping into the sea. “Because we shoot in these long takes, the most important thing was to have the emotional trajectory of the situation,” he says. “We thought a lot about how to achieve that moment in a technical way, and we thought about cranes and drones, but it wasn’t the right thing. I proposed to Cristian to test to see if I could physically jump in the water with them and we did it in a weekend and it worked.” ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Turns Chaos & Crime Into Record-Shattering Launch New ‘Friday The 13th’ Movie Unveils Cast, Title & Release Date Skydance Shakes Up Cable Biz With Four Execs Running Programs & Howard Lee Exiting Par-WB Shakeup Sees Top Roles For Kira Goldberg, Erhman; Who’s Out Read More About: Comments
